title: Finance Administrator (Accounts Payable)
description:
Finance Administrator (Accounts Payable)

Location: Yeovil, Somerset
Salary: £25,000 - £27,000 PA
Hours: Monday - Friday, 9am - 5pm (1 hour lunch)

Benefits
- 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays
- 5% Contributory Pension
- Free parking

Looking to build a career in finance?

We're recruiting for a Finance Administrator to join a friendly and supportive team of 7 in Yeovil. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with previous experience in accounts payable, finance, or administration, but we're also keen to hear from individuals who are naturally organised, enjoy working with numbers and data, and are looking to develop a career within finance.

If you're detail-oriented, proactive, and enjoy problem-solving, this could be a great next step for you.

The Role

As a Finance Administrator, you'll play an important role in supporting the day-to-day running of the finance department. You'll work closely with suppliers and colleagues across the business to ensure invoices, payments and financial records are processed accurately and efficiently.

This is a varied position where no two days are quite the same, offering plenty of opportunity to learn and develop your finance knowledge.

Key Responsibilities
- Processing and verifying supplier invoices
- Matching invoices to purchase orders and ensuring correct coding and approvals
- Preparing and assisting with supplier payment runs
- Monitoring payment deadlines and ensuring payments are made on time
- Investigating and resolving invoice queries and payment discrepancies
- Building positive relationships with suppliers and responding to enquiries
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving outstanding issues
- Maintaining accurate financial records and supporting finance administration tasks
- Working closely with colleagues across the business to support the wider finance function

About You

We're looking for someone who is:
- Organised with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable working with numbers, data and spreadsheets
- Confident communicating with colleagues, customers and suppliers
- Proactive and willing to learn
- Able to manage their workload effectively
- Reliable, positive and team-focused

Previous finance or accounts payable experience would be beneficial, but it's not essential. If you've worked in an administrative role, enjoy working with numbers, and are keen to develop a career in finance, we'd love to hear from you.

Don't Tick Every Box?

Please don't let that stop you from applying. We're interested in people with the right attitude, willingness to learn, and transferable skills just as much as direct experience. If this opportunity sounds like a good fit for you, we'd encourage you to apply.

How to Apply

To apply for this role, please do so online, email your CV to , or call Vicky on for a confidential chat.

We look forward to hearing from you.

title: P/T ACCOUNTS ADMINISTRATOR / BOOKKEEPER
description:
Somerset Solders Ltd, incorporating Somerset Workwear, is an established and growing Somerset business supplying customers across the electronics, construction, medical and transport sectors. We are looking for an experienced and dependable Accounts Administrator to join our small, friendly team. This is a varied, hands-on role with responsibility for the day-to-day accounting administration of the business.

We are offering a permanent position working 16 hours per week with a flexible approach on how the hours are worked with hybrid working to be discussed.

Key responsibilities:

Maintaining sales and purchase ledgers

Credit control and customer statements

Bank and nominal ledger reconciliations

Resolving supplier and customer invoice queries

Preparing and submitting VAT returns, ensuring VAT is correctly accounted for on transactions

Liaising with colleagues, customers and suppliers on accounts matters

Supporting month-end accounting processes / reporting to management

You ll ideally have at least two years experience in bookkeeping or a similar accounting role and be comfortable working independently across a range of day-to-day accounting tasks. Experience with Xero is essential. Previous experience in working with an ERP system will be an advantage.

We offer:

Permanent part-time position 16 hours per week

Flexible working hours to be discussed

Opportunity for some hybrid working once established in the role

Salary based on experience

Company pension

Free on-site parking

Friendly, supportive small-team environment

Training on the company ERP system

Holiday entitlement increases with length of service

We close between Christmas and New Year, usually around a week

20% staff discount off our products

If you would like to join us, please apply by emailing your CV for the attention of Caira Day

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll Administrator

Location: Yeovil

Salary: £25,000 - £30,000

Hours: Full-time or Part-time (minimum 30 hours per week)

Working Pattern: Office-based during training, with hybrid working available thereafter

Are you an experienced Payroll Administrator looking to join a friendly and supportive accountancy practice where flexibility, professional development and work-life balance are genuinely valued?

Due to continued growth, a well-established accountancy practice in Yeovil is looking to recruit a Payroll Administrator to join its busy payroll department. Working as part of a close-knit team, you'll be responsible for delivering an accurate and efficient payroll service to a diverse client portfolio while enjoying excellent support and development opportunities.

This opportunity would suit someone with previous payroll experience who enjoys building client relationships, working as part of a team and managing a varied workload in a fast-paced practice environment.

The Role

As Payroll Administrator, your responsibilities will include:
- Processing end-to-end payrolls for a portfolio of clients
- Managing weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly and monthly payrolls
- Processing starters, leavers and contractual changes
- Calculating statutory payments including SSP, SMP and SPP
- Managing pension administration and auto-enrolment duties
- Submitting RTI information to HMRC
- Handling payroll queries from clients and employees
- Maintaining accurate payroll records and ensuring compliance with payroll legislation
- Supporting colleagues within the payroll team during busy periods

About You

To be successful in this role, you'll ideally have:
- Previous payroll experience within an accountancy practice, payroll bureau or in-house payroll environment
- Knowledge of current payroll legislation and processes
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Excellent organisational and time management skills
- The ability to work effectively to deadlines
- Strong communication and customer service skills
- Experience using payroll software and Microsoft Excel

What's on Offer?

In return, you'll benefit from a supportive and flexible working environment along with an excellent benefits package, including:
- Hybrid working following a successful training and onboarding period
- Flexible working arrangements that can be tailored around personal commitments, including school runs and other family responsibilities
- Full-time or part-time hours available (minimum 30 hours per week)
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Free on-site parking
- Cycle to Work scheme
- Study support towards professional payroll qualifications, including the Level 3 CIPP qualification
- Regular staff socials and team events
- Friendly and collaborative team environment

Why Join?

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a growing and supportive accountancy practice that genuinely invests in its people. You'll become part of a small team where your contribution is recognised, whilst benefiting from flexible working arrangements, ongoing training and support towards professional payroll qualifications.

If you're looking for a role where you can continue developing your payroll career within a welcoming practice environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply online ASAP, shortlisted applicants will be contacted within 48 working hours.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Job Title: Payroll Assistant

Location: Yeovil, Somerset

Salary: 28,000 - 31,000 PA DOE

Hours: 30-37.5 hours, Monday to Friday flexible dependant on the candidate. The company also offers flexi time with 10-4 being the core hours

Benefits: 25 days plus Bank Holidays, Xmas Closure, Free Parking, Death in Service, Cycle to Work Scheme, Staff Socials, Modern Offices

Are you experienced in payroll looking for your next opportunity within a friendly and professional business? We're working with a well-established and growing accountancy practice in Yeovil who are looking to add a detail-focused payroll professional to their team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys managing payroll processes, building strong client relationships, and working in a supportive environment where accuracy and customer service are highly valued. They are always developing their staff and will fully support you with further qualifications and achieving your CIPP Level 3

The Role

As a Payroll Assistant, you'll be responsible for managing a portfolio of payroll clients and ensuring payrolls are processed accurately and on time. You'll work closely with clients, HMRC, and pension providers while ensuring all statutory deadlines are consistently met.

Key Responsibilities
- Processing weekly, fortnightly and monthly payrolls for a variety of clients
- Setting up new payroll clients and HMRC accounts
- Processing starters, leavers and payroll amendments
- Submitting RTI reports to HMRC
- Issuing employee payslips and payroll summaries to clients
- Managing auto-enrolment pension submissions and reconciliations
- Calculating and reconciling PAYE payments and Attachment of Earnings Orders
- Liaising with pension providers regarding client schemes
- Responding to payroll-related queries from clients and HMRC
- Ensuring compliance with payroll legislation and filing deadlines
- Supporting colleagues across the wider team as required
- Assisting with administrative duties, system updates and general office support
- Providing clients with up-to-date information on payroll legislation changes

About You

To be successful in this role, you'll ideally have:
- Previous payroll administration experience
- Strong understanding of payroll legislation and compliance requirements
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Confident communication skills and a professional telephone manner
- Ability to manage multiple deadlines and prioritise workloads effectively
- Strong IT skills and experience using payroll software
- A proactive approach and willingness to support the wider team

If you're an organised and reliable payroll professional looking for a new challenge, we'd love to hear from you.
